title: Machine learning for survival outcome in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a multicenter validation study.
summary: A voting model trained on SEER records predicted overall survival for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and was evaluated in German and Swedish cohorts. Its discrimination varied across cohorts; the study supports prognostic assessment, not evidence of treatment benefit.
ai_technology: Machine-learning survival models use clinicopathological and treatment-related variables, trained on SEER data and assessed in multicenter registry cohorts.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The study reports retrospective overall-survival prediction using a large SEER training set and validation cohorts in Germany and Sweden; prognostic performance does not establish treatment benefit.
evidence.unknown: Validation cohorts support retrospective survival prediction; the study does not test whether model-guided treatment changes survival or clinical decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning survival models use clinicopathological and treatment-related variables, trained on SEER data and assessed in multicenter registry cohorts.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
